messages.author: 9d82a8b6bab6bb21
messages.subject: QTLs in RILs with replicates
parts:
Hi Karl,

I had a question about how to approach using R/QTL2 for QTL analysis in a set of plant RILs. Here are some specifics:
  • Mapping population: F5 RILs by selfing
  • Genotyped and phenotyped ~300 unique lines, 2 biological replicates per line
  • Genotyped and phenotyped ~25 individuals derived from selfing the parents of the mapping population
I have taken several approaches; some of the suggestions came from combing through discussions for R/QTL and R/QTL2:
  1. Keeping all the individuals genotyped and phenotyped:
    • Linear mixed model. However, in this case, no QTL peaks are detected for the phenotype I am most interested.
    • Linear mixed model with LOCO. In this case, QTLs are detected for all traits
  2. Removing duplicates (only one individual per line; only keeping the parents):
    • HK 
    • Linear mixed model
    • Linear mixed model with LOCO
I haven't tried to take the phenotypic averages of each line, but I am planning to do that soon. I also need to do some reading into the linear mixed model and LMM-LOCO approaches to better understand what this is doing (and perhaps I shouldn't be using this approach?).

Nevertheless, there appears to be some overlap in the results from each of these approaches, which is great! But there are some inconsistencies between approaches, especially with the phenotypes I'm most interested in. 

Any suggestions and clarifications would be very much appreciated! 

Many thanks,
Irene

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] QTLs in RILs with replicates
parts:
I don't think it's clear what is the best approach for QTL analysis in RIL. Personally, I'd use LMM with LOCO using strain means, weighting the strain means by the sample size. But I think this remains a topic for research.

Working with individual values has the advantage that you can incorporate individual-level covariates in the analysis, rather than regressing them out in advance.

karl
